newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's UES makes Brevnov chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Russia's UES makes Brevnov chief executive.

text.p: Shareholders in Russia's largest company, utility UES, voted company vice-president Boris Brevnov chief executive at the annual meeting on Friday.
Brevnov, an ally of First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, who is also Energy Minister, replaces Anatoly Dyakov, who retains his second position as chairman of the board of directors.
The management shuffle is the government's latest move in its campaign, led by Nemtsov, to revamp Russia's natural monopolies, large companies like UES with no competition.

Reformers, who have promised not to break up the monopolies, aim to eliminate a huge backlog in payments between energy producers, customers and fuel suppliers and introduce an element of competition to the national wholesale markets.

UES, Russia's largest company by sales, owns and operates the national electricity transmission grid, operates 27 of Russia's 34 largest power plants and has stakes of 49 percent or more in 70 of 72 regional power utilities.

The government owns 52.7 percent of UES. Foreigners hold 28 percent, Brevnov's office said. Brevnov hails from Nemtsov's home town and was voted in by a board packed with government representatives headed by Nemtsov himself.
